title: Depth and first Fitting ideal give a quadratic completion and LCI neighbourhood
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], $\mathfrak p\subset S$ a maximal ideal, $A=S_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$, and $F=S/\mathfrak p$. Assume $F/k$ is finite separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], $\operatorname{depth}A=1$ [def-weil-pbc-depth], and $\operatorname{Fit}_1(\Omega_{S/k})A=\mathfrak m$, using Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and the index-$1$ presentation-minor ideal [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change]. Then there exist a $k$-algebra section $\sigma:F\to\widehat A$ of the residue map, $a,b,c\in F$ with $b^2-4ac\ne0$, and a continuous isomorphism of complete local $F$-algebras $\widehat A\cong F[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ inducing the identity on $F$, where $\widehat A$ is the $\mathfrak m$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], $F$ acts through $\sigma$, and power series have the variable-ideal-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Moreover, some $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak p$ has $S_g$ a local complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field].

source.place: Tags 0C4D (lemma-nodal), equivalence (5) and (2), 0C4C (lemma-fitting-ideal), 0C49 (lemma-nodal-algebraic), and 0C4E (lemma-nodal-lci), final complete-intersection paragraph.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-separable-closed-point-formal-presentation] to the given finite type algebra and maximal ideal with finite separable residue field. Put $R=\widehat A$ and $\mathfrak m_R=\mathfrak mR$. It gives Noetherian local rings $A,R$, residue field $F$, a $k$-algebra residue section $\sigma:F\to R$, and a continuous surjection $T=F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]\twoheadrightarrow R$ with $n\ge2$ and kernel $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_s)\subseteq(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$. Its Jacobian cokernel presents $\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_AR$. Fix this section and presentation throughout.

source.place: Tag 0C52 (lemma-complete-local-ring-structure-as-algebra); completed Jacobian comparison as in curves.tex, Tag 0C4D (lemma-nodal).

proof.text: Choose finite algebra generators $s_i$ of $S$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Additivity and the Leibniz rule in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] express every $\mathrm dP(s_i)$ as an $S$-linear combination of the $\mathrm ds_i$, so $\Omega_{S/k}$ is finite. By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization], its localization is $\Omega_{A/k}$, with $\mathrm d(s/t)=t^{-1}\mathrm ds-st^{-2}\mathrm dt$. Apply [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change](2) first to $S\to A$ and then to $A\to R$. The hypothesis therefore gives $\operatorname{Fit}_1(\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_AR)=\mathfrak mR=\mathfrak m_R$. In the presentation of step 1 this is precisely the ideal $J$ of $(n-1)$-minors of $(\partial f_j/\partial t_i)$: the relation module is spanned by its rows, and multilinearity expands any minor of relation rows into a linear combination of the generator-row minors. Thus $J=\mathfrak m_R$.

source.place: Tag 0C4D (lemma-nodal), Jacobian presentation and first Fitting ideal; algebra.tex Tag 00RT (lemma-differentials-localize), part (2); more-algebra.tex Tags 07Z8 and 07ZA, part (3).

proof.text: The completion map $A\to R$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat] and local because $\mathfrak mR=\mathfrak m_R$. Both rings are Noetherian by step 1, so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-depth-formula] applies. Its closed fibre is $R/\mathfrak mR=F$. This field has depth zero: its maximal ideal is zero, and multiplication by zero on the nonzero module $F$ is not injective, so only the empty regular sequence contributes in [def-weil-pbc-depth]. Consequently $\operatorname{depth}R=\operatorname{depth}A+0=1$.

source.place: Tag 07NW (lemma-completion-depth), proved using algebra.tex Tag 0337 (lemma-apply-grothendieck); flatness is algebra.tex Tag 00MC.

proof.text: For $R=T/I$, steps 2 and 3 verify condition (a) of [lem-trf-formal-jacobian-quadratic-criterion], with $F$ a field, $n\ge2$, and $I$ in the variable ideal as required. Condition (b) supplies $a,b,c\in F$ with $b^2-4ac\ne0$ and a continuous isomorphism of complete local $F$-algebras $R\cong F[[u,v]]/(Q)$, $Q=au^2+buv+cv^2$. The $F$-structure on $R$ is the fixed $\sigma$ from step 1; $F$-linearity makes the residue map of this isomorphism the identity on $F$. This proves the quadratic-completion assertion with its required normalization.

source.place: Tag 0C4C (lemma-fitting-ideal), implication (3) to (1); Tag 0C49 (lemma-nodal-algebraic), implication (2) to (3).

proof.text: The discriminant inequality implies that $a,b,c$ are not all zero, hence $Q\ne0$ by its coefficients. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-domain], $F[[u,v]]$ is a domain, so multiplication by $Q$ is injective. Also $Q\in(u,v)^2$, and evaluation at $u=v=0$ induces a surjection $F[[u,v]]/(Q)\twoheadrightarrow F$, so this quotient is nonzero. Thus $(Q)$ is a regular sequence of length one in $(u,v)$ by [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. The isomorphism of step 4 verifies condition (2) of [lem-trf-completion-local-complete-intersection] with $r=2,c=1$. Its condition (1) gives $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak p$ with $S_g$ a local complete intersection over $k$, as required.
